To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Casimir effect is significant for quark-gluons confined in a slab with a width of about 1 fm and that the Casimir energy and entropy densities are enhanced by a factor of 2∼4.

(i) the Casimir energy and entropy of the quark-gluun plasma in the slab region are large when the width of region is about one Fermi and (ii) the Casimir effect is important in the confinement of quark-gluuon plasma.
the Casimir effect is important in the confinement region and the Casimir effect increases the energy and entropy densities by a factor of 2∼4 at the transition temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Casimir effect in the early stage of relativistic heavy ion collisions.
the Casimir effect of the QGP.
the Casimir effect in a slab region on baryon free quark-gluons plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Casimir effect in the QGP phase is not large enough to be observed in heavy ion collisions at RHIC or LHC.
the Casimir effect is not negligible in the confinement of QGP in a slab region.
the Casimir effect can be important in a QGP confined in a finite region, but it is not a dominant factor in determining its physical properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Casimir effect is important to the thermodynamical property of confined QGP.
the Casimir effect can be important to the thermodynamic properties of confined QGP.
the Casimir effect is a significant factor in the QCD phase transition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Casimir energy of QGP is comparable to the thermal energy at high temperatures.
the Casimir effect may be an important factor for determining the equation of state of QGP.
the Casimir effect can enhance the energy density of QGP by 2∼ 3 times.
